source: make a shooting game with a sliding,crouching, dashing mechanics and include assault rifles, snipers, revolvers, shotguns, pistols and make them do a fair amount of damage each and make a battle arena for ppl to fight in and if u die I respawn and first person to get the most kills wins and each kill gives the player 10 coins and coins will be used to open weapon boxes and each win gives 50 coins and the weapon boxes will cost 150 coin and the players with fight for 2 minutes and 30 seconds

answers.ask: No look was stated - military, sci-fi, or bright and arcade?
answers.answer: Use a military-themed battle arena with clear, practical cover and readable weapon designs.

answers.ask: How many players fight at once? A 2:30 free-for-all plays very differently at 6 players than at 20, and that sets the arena size.
answers.answer: Make it a 6-player free-for-all so the arena can stay compact and fast-paced.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No look was stated - military, sci-fi, or bright and arcade? A: Use a military-themed battle arena with clear, practical cover and readable weapon designs.
- [author] scale — Q: How many players fight at once? A 2:30 free-for-all plays very differently at 6 players than at 20, and that sets the arena size. A: Make it a 6-player free-for-all so the arena can stay compact and fast-paced.
- [agent_inferred] arena circulation — Q: How should a compact free-for-all avoid dead-end spawn traps? A: Use a small interconnected lane network with loops and several ways into the central fight space.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a compact military-themed battle arena for a six-player free-for-all. Organize practical waist-high and full-body cover along a small interconnected network of looping combat lanes, with several approaches into a central clash area and no dead-end spawn pockets. Keep sightlines readable for assault rifles, snipers, revolvers, shotguns, and pistols, balancing short cover-to-cover routes with a few longer firing corridors. Place six screened start pockets around the arena perimeter so no player appears directly in another player's line of fire.

## Genre
The genre is Shooter because ranged weapon combat, kill scoring, respawning, and a timed free-for-all define the game.

## Shape and preset
Use `lane-network`, with compact interconnected routes channeling all six players toward recurring engagement fronts. Match the Arena Deathmatch preset while dropping unrequested map pickups and elevated nests; retain the looping circulation and adapt the starts for free-for-all rather than teams.

## Config requirements
Use `cover-los` for evenly distributed practical military cover, `path-loop` for interconnected routes with multiple exits, `choke-bottleneck` for restrained lane junctions that focus fights without becoming spawn traps, and `spawn-protected` for six screened perimeter start pockets.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly six `spawn-protected` SpawnZones around the perimeter, separated from one another and shielded from direct sniper sightlines into adjacent starts while retaining quick access to the central lanes. Kill counting, respawn timing, weapon damage, currency rewards, weapon-box prices, and the 2-minute-30-second round clock are gameplay mechanics rather than layout placements.

## Layout components
The build contains six perimeter spawn pockets, several short looping lanes, one central clash zone, practical waist-high and full-body cover, narrow lane junctions, and a hard arena boundary. Keep routes compact, eliminate dead ends, and compose the central combat area and all lane entries clearly in frame.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: balanced six-way spawn separation, looping circulation, and readable firing corridors should be authoritative before the military isometric dressing.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small because the six-player arena is explicitly compact and its individual cover pieces and sightlines must remain legible. The theme is a practical military combat arena. `P0` applies because all requested play occurs on one bounded surface without overhangs, interiors, separate maps, or procedural-validity requirements.
